# #694 — Server: stateless /mcp request path beside the handshake path (no session id, no initialize)

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: enhancement
Created: 2026-08-09T17:30:48Z
Updated: 2026-08-09T17:30:48Z

---

Part of #692. Blocked by #693 (the charter names the SDK version and the
dual-protocol shape this ticket implements).

## What exists today

`POST /mcp` has exactly two outcomes (`server/transport/session-manager.ts:226-287`):
an `mcp-session-id` header that matches a live entry, or an `isInitializeRequest`
body that mints one. Anything else is a hard `400 "Bad request: missing session
or not an initialize request"`. A stateless RC client sends neither — no
`Mcp-Session-Id`, no `initialize` — so **every RC-conformant request currently
gets a 400**. That is the gap, and it is one branch.

## Scope

Add a stateless request path alongside the session path, not instead of it.

- `server/transport/session-manager.ts:226-234` — the third branch: no session
  id, not an initialize request, `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28` present ->
  build a per-request transport, serve, discard. No entry in `sessions`, no
  timer, no cap consumption, no `pendingInitializes`.
- **Identity per request.** The session path binds `AuthIdentity` once at
  initialize and re-checks it with `sameIdentity` (`:68-76`) on every
  subsequent call. Stateless has nothing to compare against: the auth
  middleware's identity IS the identity, and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo"]`
  is client-asserted metadata that MUST NOT be trusted for authorization.
  Write the test that proves a `_meta` clientInfo cannot widen a token's
  namespace or role — this is the security seam of the whole epic.
- `server/transport/http-app.ts:96-112` — routing unchanged for POST; GET
  and DELETE behavior when the caller is stateless (a stateless client has no
  session to DELETE and no SSE stream to GET).
- `src/index.ts:270-292` + `src/transport.ts` — the rollback entrypoint. The
  charter (#693) decides whether it gets the stateless path too or is frozen;
  this ticket implements that decision and states which was chosen.
- Both entrypoints keep the handshake path working unchanged. Zero behavior
  change for a client that still sends `initialize`.

## Explicitly deferred to sibling tickets

Headers/caching/errors -> the header+cache ticket. Deletion of the session
machinery -> the deletion ticket. This one only makes a stateless request
succeed.

## Done means

`scripts/done-means/NNN-stateless-request-path.sh`, written red-first, drives
the real HTTP surface (not a unit mock) and asserts:

1. `POST /mcp` with a valid bearer token, `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28`,
   NO `Mcp-Session-Id`, and a `tools/call` body returns 200 with a valid
   result. Fails today with 400.
2. The response carries NO `Mcp-Session-Id` header.
3. `sessionCount()` and `pendingInitializeCount()` are unchanged before and
   after N stateless calls — proves no slot consumption.
4. `maxSessions` stateless calls succeed with the cap set to 1 — proves the
   cap does not gate the stateless path.
5. A full legacy `initialize` -> `tools/call` -> `DELETE` cycle still passes
   on the same head — the transition guarantee.
6. A stateless request whose `_meta` clientInfo claims a different
   namespace/role than its token is served with the TOKEN's scope, not the
   claimed one.

Assertions 1-4 and 6 fail on today's tree; 5 passes today and must keep
passing. Controller re-runs in a fresh `lane-bootstrap` worktree before merge.

## Risk to carry into review

The session path's identity re-check exists because a session outlives the
request that created it. Removing the session does not remove the need to
scope every call to its token — it moves that duty to the auth middleware,
which now has no second line of defense behind it. Namespace isolation is a
security boundary in this repo (AGENTS.md); assertion 6 is the regression
test that boundary requires.
